newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index falls to 87.0 in March.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index falls to 87.0 in March.

text.p: The Conference Board's U.S. help-wanted advertising index fell two points to 87.0 in March from a revised 89.0 in February, the Conference Board said on Thursday.
"Demand for labor remains strong and may even be gaining more vibrancy," said Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein.
He said job and income growth, associated with a high level of household optimism, suggests "continued robust consumer spending through 1997."
Goldstein said job growth will probably increase to about 300,000 net new jobs per month over the next six to nine months.

In the last three months, the volume of help-wanted advertising rose in six of the nine U.S. regions. The greatest increase was in the Pacific region, up 11.2 percent. Other regional increases were in the Middle Atlantic, up 6.6 percent, West South Central, up 4.9 percent and South Atlantic, up 4.2 percent.
Regional declines were in East North Central, -2.6 percent, West North Central, -2.5 percent and Mountain, -0.5 percent.
